summary: Defines a YANG data model for the rules used by Static Context Header Compression and fragmentation. This makes it easier for different SCHC instances to exchange rule sets or change rule parameters in an interoperable way.

eli5.summary: SCHC squeezes messages using a shared rule book. This document is a standard format for writing that rule book so devices can swap it.

questions: how to exchange schc compression rules
what is a yang data model for schc
how are schc fragmentation rules described
subtitle: A machine-readable format for the rules that tell constrained devices how to squeeze and fragment packets.

tldr.problem: SCHC compresses and fragments packets on constrained networks using a shared set of Rules, but RFC 8724 only describes those Rules informally. Two ends cannot reliably exchange or edit them that way.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9363 defines a YANG module, ietf-schc, that describes compression Rules and fragmentation Rules with the same fields and identifiers on both ends, including the field identifier, length, position, direction, target value, matching operator and action.
tldr.outcome: SCHC instances can describe the same Rules identically, push a full set of Rules to the other end, or change specific values such as an IPv6 prefix. The RFC has since been updated by RFC 9441.

today: RFC 9363 is a Proposed Standard published in March 2023, and it is updated by RFC 9441. It builds on the SCHC framework in RFC 8724.

sections.title: Why SCHC Rules Need a Data Model
sections.content:
SCHC (Static Context Header Compression) is a compression and fragmentation mechanism for constrained networks, defined in RFC 8724. It rests on a static context that two entities at the edge of the constrained network share. That context is a set of Rules, used either for compression and decompression (C/D) or for fragmentation and reassembly (F/R).

RFC 8724 gives only an informal picture of the Rules. RFC 9363 formalizes it so that both ends have the same definition even if their internal representation differs, and so that one end can update the other with specific values such as an IPv6 prefix or a destination address.

The vehicle is a YANG data model, as defined in RFC 7950. One model covers both compression and fragmentation Rules, so every element of a Rule has a common representation. The RFC points to another document, listed as [LPWAN-ARCH], for an illustration of exchanging Rules with the model.
sections.eli5: Imagine two friends who talk in a secret shorthand. If they only half remember the shorthand, they get confused. This document writes the shorthand down in one exact format so both always agree.

sections.title: How Identifiers and Conventions Work
sections.content:
Every identifier in the model is a YANG identityref, which gives global uniqueness and makes it easy to extend later. The recipe has three steps: define a main identity whose name ends in base-type, derive all the real identities from it, then create a typedef from that base. The RFC shows this with the Reassembly Check Sequence (RCS) algorithms, where rcs-crc32 is the default RCS from RFC 8724 and is 4 bytes long.

Each kind of value then has a naming convention. A header field is named with fid- plus the protocol and field name, and every field MUST be identified through a global identityref derived from fid-base-type. Field Length uses fl- names for functions such as var (from RFC 8724) and tkl (from RFC 8824, for the CoAP Token Length). The Matching Operator uses mo-, the Compression Decompression Action uses cda-, and the Direction Indicator uses di names.

The model includes the field definitions found in RFC 8724 and RFC 8824. Field Position is a uint8 whose default is 1 and which counts repeated occurrences; the value 0 means the position is not considered when a Rule is selected.
sections.eli5: Every word in the rule book has a name tag with a fixed pattern, like labelling every lunchbox with the owner's name first. That way nobody ever grabs the wrong thing.

sections.title: Compression Rules in the Model
sections.content:
A Rule is identified by a RuleID, which is a RuleID value together with a RuleID length. A length of 0 is allowed and stands for an implicit Rule. RFC 8724 defines three natures of Rule, and the model introduces one identity for each: nature-compression, nature-no-compression (the default Rule used to send a packet whole when no compression Rule matches) and nature-fragmentation. The RuleID length and value together form the key used to look up a Rule.

A compression Rule is a list of entries, one per header field, indexed by Field ID, position and direction. Each entry holds the Field Length, a Target Value, a Matching Operator (MO) and a Compression Decompression Action (CDA). RFC 8724 defines 4 MOs and 7 CDAs. The Target Value is a list of left-aligned binary sequences, indexed from 0. For the equal and MSB operators it holds a single element, and for match-mapping it can hold several, with indexes starting at 0 and being contiguous.

The model adds two checks. When the MO is ignore no Target Value is needed, but for other MOs there MUST be one. When the MSB MO is used, the matching-operator-value must be present.

The module conforms to the Network Management Datastore Architecture of RFC 8342. Its top level is a schc container holding a list of rule entries keyed by rule-id-value and rule-id-length.
sections.eli5: A Rule is like a recipe card with a number on it. Each line says which part of a message to look at, what it should look like, and what to do about it, such as skip sending it because the other side already knows it.

sections.title: Fragmentation Rules in the Model
sections.content:
Fragmentation is optional in the model and depends on the fragmentation feature. Because a fragmentation Rule works in one direction, it MUST carry a Direction Indicator, and bidirectional MUST NOT be used.

RFC 8724 defines three fragmentation modes. In No ACK nothing is acknowledged. In ACK Always each window must be acknowledged before the next. In ACK on Error a window is acknowledged only when the receiver sees missing fragments. The model also captures the fragment header fields (the DTag, the window W and the Fragment Compressed Number FCN), the RCS carried in the last fragment, and, for ACK-on-Error, whether the last fragment carries no tile, one tile, or leaves it to the sender.

Two timers need a range wider than RFC 8724 gives, so the model uses a tick. The duration of a tick is 2^(tick-duration)/10^6 seconds. With the default tick-duration of 20 the unit is 1.048575 seconds, and the timers can cover a range from 1.0 second to 19 hours, as RFC 9011 recommends. The retransmission timer, if specified, MUST be strictly positive; an inactivity timer of 0 means it is disabled.

Other parameters include max-ack-requests, l2-word-size (default 8 bits; a value of 1 means no alignment and no padding) and maximum-packet-size (default 1280 bytes).
sections.eli5: When a message is too big to fit in one envelope, it is cut into pieces. These rules say how many envelopes to send, whether the receiver says thanks after each batch, and how long to wait before giving up.

sections.title: A Worked Example
sections.content:
The appendix takes three informal Rules and writes them out in XML using the model. Rule 6/3 is a compression Rule for IPv6 headers. For instance, the IPv6 version field is 4 bits, bidirectional, matched with mo-equal against 6 and handled with cda-not-sent, so it costs nothing on the wire. The payload length is ignored by matching and recomputed with cda-compute, and the application prefix and interface identifier are sent as values.

Rule 12/11 is a fragmentation Rule in No ACK mode with a DTag of 2 bits, a window of 0 bits and an FCN of 3 bits, using the CRC32 RCS. Rule 100/8 is a no-compression Rule.
sections.eli5: The example shows a real recipe card written in the exact format. Some lines say do not send this part at all, because both sides already know it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The module is meant to be accessed with network management protocols such as NETCONF or RESTCONF, which run over secure transports (SSH and TLS respectively), and the Network Configuration Access Control Model can restrict who may read or write which data.

The writable /schc nodes are sensitive. A Rule can contain, for instance, the application IPv6 address where a device's data goes after decompression, so an attacker who changes another device's Rules could block communication or enable eavesdropping. A device must therefore be allowed to modify only its own Rules on the remote SCHC instance, and the requester's identity must be validated, for example with certificates or access lists. Some fields should not be modified at all: IPv6 address descriptors should not be changed, while a UDP device port could be.

Reading the Rules is also sensitive, because an attacker could learn the traffic a device generates, its application addresses or its REST API.
sections.eli5: The rule book says where a device's messages go. If a stranger could rewrite it, your messages could be sent to the wrong place, so only the owner may change their own pages, and snoopers should not read them.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA registered the URI urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-schc in the IETF XML Registry. It also registered the YANG module in the YANG Module Names registry with the name ietf-schc, the prefix schc and RFC 9363 as the reference. The module file in the RFC is named ietf-schc@2023-03-01.yang.
sections.eli5: The module got an official name and address in a public list, so nobody else can claim the same one.

viz.caption: WHAT EACH COMPRESSION RULE ENTRY HOLDS

cells: Which protocol field the entry applies to
Size in bits, or a function such as var or tkl
Which occurrence of the field; 0 means do not care
Value the header field is matched against
How the field is compared with the Target Value
How the field is compressed and restored

items.label: No acknowledgment
items.desc: Unidirectional; no acknowledgment is sent back.

items.label: Every window acknowledged
items.desc: Each window must be acknowledged before going to the next.

items.label: Acknowledge on missing fragments
items.desc: A window is acknowledged only when the receiver detects missing fragments.
